newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.04 pct in calm trading.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.04 pct in calm trading.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.04 percent to end at 1.0165 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market in calm trading after the Central Bank confirmed the real-dollar mini-band set late Thursday, dealers said.
Early today, the Central Bank confirmed the trade level for the real by buying dollars at 1.016 and selling at 1.021 reais per greenback through a buy/sell auction.
After the tender, a Central Bank spokesman told Reuters the bank intended to maintain the mini-band unchanged throughout Friday.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a Friday surplus of around $50 million.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real dropped 0.05 percent to end at 1.0211 to the dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real rose 0.29 percent to end at 1.029 reais per dollar, mostly due to an increase in dollar supply, traders said.
